video.title: Every successful startup starts with this one advantage

summary: Jeff Harmon (Harmon Brothers ad agency, co-founder of Angel Studios) tells My First Million hosts how he built marketing campaigns for Orbrush, Poopourri, Squatty Potty and Purple Mattress, and how Angel Studios funds and markets films through a member 'guild'. The central framework is 'find your glitch': spot a channel or market gap others ignore, such as early YouTube ads costing under a penny a view, and use it as a beachhead. He also covers a comedian-led ad creation retreat, celebrity face-warming for algorithms, vibe-coding with agents overnight, and mindset lessons about letting go of disputes. Most figures are self-reported and the transcript is auto-generated with some errors.

speakers.name: Jeff Harmon
speakers.description: Co-founder of Harmon Brothers ad agency and Angel Studios; author of Poop to Gold

speakers.name: Sam Parr / Shaan Puri (My First Million hosts, names not stated in transcript)

ideas.name: Orbrush tongue cleaner via YouTube direct response
ideas.one_liner: Sell a tongue cleaner online using a $500 comedic explainer video and cheap early YouTube ads, with a free-plus-shipping offer.
ideas.business_model: One-off product sales; free product with shipping charged at cost-plus
ideas.customer: People worried about bad breath, online buyers
ideas.problem: People cannot tell if they have bad breath and tongue is source of about 90% of it
ideas.offer: A tongue cleaner brush, free if you pay shipping, promoted with a 'how to tell if you have bad breath' video

pricing.model: Free product plus shipping charge set to cover product cost
pricing.notes: Shipping charged roughly what it cost to buy the brush

acquisition_channels.details: Launched a ~$500 scripted video and bought YouTube ads at under a penny per view in YouTube's early ad days; spend $1 to bring in $2-3.

quote.text: those ads cost less than a penny per view. So it's like the early days of ad sense.
quote.speaker: Jeff Harmon

acquisition_channels.details: Earlier attempt: bought a 1.3M-follower Facebook page 'Kisses' for $5,000 and rebranded it; failed to sell much. Google ads also cost $3-5 per $1 of sales.

ideas.delivery: Physical product shipped from stock (Dr. Bob had thousands of units); site coded by Harmon's brother
unit_economics_claims: Spend $1 total (ads, shipping, brush) to bring in $2-3
ideas.startup_cost: About $500 for the video plus $5,000 for the failed Facebook page

acquisition.how: Paid ads are largely automatable, though the early-YouTube arbitrage no longer exists.

delivery.how: Physical stock shipped; needs fulfilment partner or human.

support.how: Order queries and returns can be agent-handled.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK with Meta/YouTube ads and fulfilment; the early cheap ad window has closed.

risks: Cheap ad channel advantage disappears as costs rise

quotes.text: Partially like going back in time, I found a glitch in the system, and everybody who starts a business, you have to find your glitch.
quotes.speaker: Jeff Harmon

quotes.text: we were able to spend a dollar and bring in two or three dollars now, a dollar in total costs
quotes.speaker: Jeff Harmon

ideas.name: Harmon Brothers viral ad agency
ideas.one_liner: Comedian-written, formula-based long-form video ads for consumer brands (Poopourri, Squatty Potty, Purple Mattress).
ideas.problem: Brands struggle to get attention and sales for products
ideas.offer: Scripted funny video ads built on a problem/solution/credibility/CTA structure, created in a 3-4 day retreat

pricing.notes: Hinted at possible performance-linked payment: 'we probably wouldn't have been paid'

acquisition_channels.details: Reputation from prior campaigns and book Poop to Gold; clients like Suzy Batiz of Poopourri reached out by email.

ideas.delivery: 3-4 writers/comedians receive product weeks ahead; retreat day 1 script reads, pick lead script, cannibalise others over 3 days; then produce the ad and run it on YouTube
unit_economics_claims: Poopourri was doing about $4M/yr when they started

delivery.how: Comedic creative and filming need humans; AI could draft scripts only.

uk_applicability.notes: Agency model transfers; humour and market differ.

quotes.text: it's way easier to train a median to be a marketer than it is to train a marketer to be funny.
quotes.speaker: Jeff Harmon

ideas.name: Angel Studios / Angel Guild
ideas.one_liner: Values-based film and TV studio funded by a ~3M-member paid guild who vote on films, get tickets and share profits with filmmakers.
ideas.business_model: Membership subscription ($12-20/month) plus film distribution profit split with filmmakers
ideas.customer: Families wanting values-based entertainment without sex or strong language; independent filmmakers
ideas.problem: Hollywood content too nihilistic/vulgar; ~1,000 independent movies a year lack a home
ideas.offer: Members vote on films, get two movie tickets per release, give feedback; filmmakers get distribution with 50% of profits

pricing.notes: Rely on breakage since average person attends 3-4 movies a year

acquisition_channels.details: Large ad spend to acquire members; film launches cost $5-20M in ads over 90 days.
Celebrity-led campaigns (Kevin James as Matt Taylor) reaching over a billion views.
Community of members who vote and promote films.

ideas.delivery: Distribute independent films to theatres and streaming; filmmakers fund production

acquisition.how: Ads and content can be heavily tooled but creative needs humans.

delivery.how: Film production and theatre distribution are physical and human.

uk_applicability.notes: Capital-intensive and tied to US values-based audience; not a solo-founder model.

quotes.text: you get two movie tickets to every movie the angel releases
quotes.speaker: Jeff Harmon

ideas.name: The Chosen crowdfunding via 19-minute YouTube ad
ideas.one_liner: Upload a 19-minute pilot as a skippable YouTube ad, then ask viewers to invest; raised $11M from 17,000 people.
ideas.problem: Funding a TV series outside Hollywood
ideas.offer: Invest in the series after watching the pilot

acquisition_channels.details: 19-minute pilot run as skippable ads; $800,000 ad spend for $11M raised; plus a 24-48 hour live-stream marathon with live social proof pop-ups.

quote.text: 17,000 people invested 11 million dollars into the chosen.
quote.speaker: Jeff Harmon

acquisition.how: Ads can be automated; live stream needs humans.

uk_applicability.notes: Equity crowdfunding is regulated by the FCA; large production budgets.

quotes.text: even if only 3% of people make it to the end, if they're the ones that want it to exist, they're going to invest
quotes.speaker: Jeff Harmon

ideas.name: VidAngel content filtering
ideas.one_liner: Service that scrubs sex, nudity and language from existing movies, a legal alternative to clean torrents.

uk_applicability.notes: Copyright issues are severe; the company faced legal problems.

ideas.name: Agentic shopping optimisation
ideas.one_liner: Make a store API-accessible so AI shopping agents can buy directly without scraping.

acquisition_channels.details: Optimise for AI agent shopping channels such as Grok.

quotes.text: you can plug into this huge growing rapidly growing group of people that are wanting to shop through their bots
quotes.speaker: Jeff Harmon

ideas.name: Celebrity face-warming social campaigns
ideas.one_liner: Launch a fresh character account using a celebrity's face so platforms push it to their audience.
ideas.offer: Persona accounts with thousands of clips

acquisition_channels.details: Cut thousands of videos for Kevin James/Matt Taylor character; campaign claimed over a billion views.

ideas.delivery: Team lived with Kevin James producing content

quotes.text: we probably cut thousands of videos to try to get a few of them to go off.
quotes.speaker: Jeff Harmon

ideas.name: Personal vibe coder / overnight agent prototyping
ideas.one_liner: Executives hire a personal coder and run AI agents overnight to prototype products.
ideas.offer: Prototype tools via agents and harnesses
ideas.delivery: Agents run plans overnight within guardrail harnesses

quotes.text: I end up vibe coding till I break something and then the engineering team builds a new harness to fix what I broke.
quotes.speaker: Jeff Harmon

ideas.name: Trailer A/B testing tool
ideas.one_liner: AI-built tool that randomly serves different trailers to friends and family to find the best one.

tactics.name: Beachhead on a small segment
steps: Identify a niche of a few percent of the market that wants the product
Treat that millions-strong segment as enough to clear inventory or launch

quote.text: 8% of people is like 30 million people just in the United States.
quote.speaker: Jeff Harmon

tactics.name: Skippable long-form ad as a filter
steps: Make entertaining content long enough to build investment
Run as skippable ad so only interested viewers watch
End with a call to action such as invest or buy

tactics.name: Comedian-led ad retreat
steps: Send product to 3-4 writers weeks ahead
Day 1 read scripts and pick the lead
Cut any joke that does not advance the message
Lock all stakeholders in so approvals happen on-site

tactics.name: Live social proof during fundraising
steps: Run a 24-48 hour live-stream marathon at the end of the raise
Pop up each new investment in real time with amount and location

tactics.name: Sell the benefit not the product
steps: Frame the product as a tool to the desired outcome (kissing without bad-breath shame)

tactics.name: Warm a celebrity face in the algorithm
steps: Have the celebrity repost older content to heat the face
Cut thousands of clips and take many swings

tools_mentioned.name: YouTube ads
tools_mentioned.cost_stated: Under a penny per view in early days

warnings.warning: Early YouTube ad arbitrage no longer exists; the glitch constantly shifts.

quote.text: YouTube ads are not a penny anymore. So that specific glitch is always changing, right?
quote.speaker: Host

warnings.warning: Early Orbrush Facebook page spamming and Google ads failed with ads costing $3-5 per $1 of sales.

quote.text: that failed miserably. We didn't sell hardly anything.
quote.speaker: Jeff Harmon

warnings.warning: Lawsuits over unpaid invoices can drain 18 months to 3 years; mentor said unless over $5M it is not worth fighting.

quote.text: unless it's worth over five million dollars, it's not even worth fighting the battle over.
quote.speaker: Jeff Harmon

warnings.warning: The movie business is a knife fight and Angel has been losing money while acquiring members.

lessons.lesson: Find a glitch: a channel or market where attention is underpriced and incumbents are not looking.

quote.text: look for things for areas where you have attention from people that nobody else is paying attention to.
quote.speaker: Jeff Harmon

lessons.lesson: Build products that solve your own problem (the user method); many top companies began that way.
Small niches can build large businesses; two million paying members is enough.
Test cheaply with real behaviour (skippable ad watch-through) to get signal before investing.
Earn attention first: let people skip, and you win those who stay.
Advertising spend of 8-12% is comparable to Wall Street raise fees; paid ads for fundraising is rational.
Letting go of disputes and keeping an abundance mentality frees focus for new opportunities.

quote.text: letting that go, change the trajectory of my life
quote.speaker: Jeff Harmon

lessons.lesson: AI harnesses with guardrails let executives run agents unattended overnight; the bottleneck is human bandwidth.
Cutting staff because of AI is a short-term play; productivity gains justify more hiring.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand storytelling by a credible operator, but numbers are recalled loosely (Orbrush revenue not remembered), Whisper tiny transcript, and mostly large-scale media businesses not replicable by a solo founder.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Guest is co-founder of Angel Studios and author of Poop to Gold; a Stardust Story sponsor read appears and is ignored.
